note: A cost PLAN against the promoted 245-row census. No provider was called, no cohort was authorised, no ledger row was written. Every unit price below is an OBSERVED rate from a completed run in another market, never a vendor list price.

classification_meanings.REUSABLE_POLICY_EVIDENCE: Evidence on file awaiting a decision. Detroit has none outstanding: the Pass 3 packet was fully applied, so its rows are ALREADY_ANSWERED or holds.
classification_meanings.SAME_METHOD_ALREADY_FAILED: The two source-silent holds. Their own site states no policy anywhere, so the same lane cannot answer them and buying it again would be a same-method retry.
classification_meanings.ROUTING_REPAIR_REQUIRED: Identity is not confirmed; nothing may bind to it yet.
classification_meanings.URL_KNOWN_POLICY_NOT_ACQUIRED: A confirmed identity with a ROUTING_CONFIRMED page and no policy yet. The cohort.
classification_meanings.URL_MISSING: A confirmed identity with no official page. Not an acquisition problem -- there is nothing to buy. Discovery/routing first, at $0 from the local extract.
classification_meanings.GENUINELY_NEW: A confirmed identity carrying a URL that routing has not yet confirmed. Payable only once routing confirms it.

cross_run_ledger.meaning: Detroit has never bought a page. Nothing in this cohort is a re-buy.

payable_cohort.lane_basis: Marriott and Hilton refuse the cheap lane and need the managed browser; every other brand is Firecrawl-reachable. Established by the acquisition pilots, not re-derived here.

discovery_needed.recommended_lane: the local OSM extract and attended reads, at $0
discovery_needed.why_not_places: Google Places is a paid discovery lane and this market has a committed local extract that has never been exhausted. Places is not warranted until a $0 pass has been run and reported.

projected_spend.basis: Observed per-attempt rates from Indianapolis (Firecrawl) and Pittsburgh (Bright Data), denominated in ATTEMPTS rather than successes -- a failed fetch costs the same as a good one.

recommended_next_hard_cap.reasoning: Roughly a third of the full cohort. Detroit has never spent, and the first paid pass in a market is also the measurement that tells you what its real yield is -- Grand Rapids bought 20 URLs for $1.70 and Pittsburgh 92 attempts for $17.08. Cap a first pass, read the yield, then size the rest on the Wilson LOWER bound of what was observed rather than on this projection.

nothing_was_run: no cohort authorised, no cap approved

withheld_from_this_plan.why: Not in the census, so not payable. They need a NAME first, which an attended read of their own property page supplies at $0.
